solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Intense blow wrought sporting injury

indicators.note: wrought means worked or fashioned, so the two words before it are reshaped into new letters

explanation.surface: A fierce blow has caused someone a sports injury.
explanation.definitionFit: This painful tendon strain is named after a racket sport, so it is a classic sporting injury.

clue.text: Urge late critic developed to get instrument

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An urge, which a belated critic has acquired, to get hold of an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges URGE, LATE and CRITIC together.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplified stringed instrument played in rock bands is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Idea with time I abandoned in middle of day

indicators.note: abandoned says the time letter and the I are dropped from the idea word

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a plan at midday, having run out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes T and I out of NOTION, leaving N-O-O-N.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock is the midpoint of the day, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Dagger, note, left in fight

indicators.note: in says the note and the left letter go inside the fight word

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scrap
TI is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A dagger is noted as left behind in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: A set-to is a British informal word for a scrap or brawl; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a slim, sharp-pointed knife, a kind of dagger.

clue.text: Measure taken at sea in alliance

definitions.meaning: a nautical unit of distance, about three miles
a union of states or clubs formed for a common purpose

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old unit of distance used at sea and a grouping of allies.

clue.text: In the past, a circle joined by Northern Anglicans

parts.note: a circle is the letter O, its shape
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Long ago a ring was joined by northern churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at one time: something done once happened in the past.

clue.text: Place requiring stiff observance?

parts.note: stiff suggests formal, rigid manners, but a stiff is slang for a corpse, laid out where mourners pay respects

explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker's premises are where the dead are kept and viewed before burial.

clue.text: One with a lot of influence in Victoria, say, gets contract

indicators.note: in says the one and the shortened influence word go inside the railway word

parts.note: Victoria is a London railway station, here an example of one
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: a lot of, not all of, so the last letter of the influence word is cut

parts.note: pull means influence or clout

explanation.surface: A powerful figure in an Australian state lands a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria looks like the Australian state or the queen, but it is a major London railway terminus; 'a lot of' cuts the last letter and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipulation is a condition laid down in an agreement, so it stands for a term of contract.

clue.text: Bank facility is put back in store by a titled figure reportedly

indicators.note: in says the turned letters go inside the store word

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: put back says the two letters of is are turned around
reportedly means as said aloud, so a count gives a word sounding the same

parts.note: a count is a nobleman, a titled figure

explanation.surface: A bank service is returned to storage by a nobleman, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns IS into SI; 'reportedly' signals that 'a count' is heard, not spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A savings account paying interest is a service a bank offers its customers.

clue.text: Bits of food generated outspoken surprised expression

indicators.note: outspoken here means spoken out loud, so the generated word gives one sounding the same

parts.note: generated means produced, as offspring are bred
crumbs is a mild British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Some food produced a blunt and astonished remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' looks like an adjective meaning frank, but signals a word said aloud. 'Crumbs!' is an old-fashioned British exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny fragments of a loaf, used for coating or stuffing, are small pieces of food.

clue.text: Speed of car at event

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken from within the following words, crossing their boundaries

explanation.surface: How fast a car goes at a race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Rate is a measure of how fast something moves, a synonym of speed.

clue.text: Archdeacon facing American space traveller

parts.note: VEN, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A churchman meets an American astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet travels through space on its orbit, so the planet is a playful space traveller.

clue.text: Preserve part of castle

definitions.meaning: the strongest central tower of a castle

explanation.definitionFit: One word means to retain or maintain something and also names a castle's fortified main tower.

clue.text: Sweltering area undressed Nordics appreciate principally

definitions.text: Sweltering area undressed Nordics appreciate principally

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Scandinavians enjoy a hot room while naked, above all.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of the five words before 'principally' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finnish steam room is a hot space where bathers sit unclothed, much loved in the Nordic countries.

clue.text: Top Forty in Rome on radio

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than read, so the numeral is spoken

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Number one in the pop charts in Italy, as broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Forty' reads as a chart, but 'Top' is the verb and 'Forty in Rome' gives XL, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To top others is to outdo them, which is what it means to be outstanding at something.

clue.text: Foreigner largely full of hypocritical talk in Spanish city

indicators.note: full of says the hypocritical talk sits inside the shortened foreigner word
largely means mostly, so the foreigner word loses its last letter

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner
cant is insincere, hypocritical talk

explanation.surface: A foreign visitor talking pious nonsense in a Spanish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the final N of the foreigner word, leaving ALIE; 'full of' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a port city on the Costa Blanca in south-eastern Spain.

clue.text: Neat queue to get soup

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
to tail is to follow in line, as a queue does

explanation.surface: A tidy line forms for soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an archaic word for cattle, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A broth made from the tail of cattle is a well-known British soup.

clue.text: Soldier finding two rivers entering part of sea?

indicators.note: entering says the two river pieces go inside the sea word

parts.note: coral forms reefs, a part of the sea, hence the question mark
the Po is an Italian river
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A soldier discovers two rivers flowing into a stretch of ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The Po is Italy's longest river; the question mark admits that coral is only loosely part of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a non-commissioned army rank, a soldier just above lance corporal.

clue.text: Persuasive man in business?

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A convincing businessman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and convincing, which is what persuasive means.

clue.text: House no type built as a centre of attraction

indicators.note: built means constructed, so the two words before it are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A house of no particular style constructed as a showpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' looks like part of the house's description but is the anagram signal; 'as a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a jar that draws bees, a honeypot is a place or thing that draws many people.

clue.text: Follow holder of money around university

indicators.note: around says the money holder wraps the university letter

parts.note: a purse holds money

explanation.surface: Track down a wallet belonging to a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the money holder round U.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue is to chase or go after, so it means to follow.

clue.text: Army division kept back by government in unrest

indicators.note: kept back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A regiment restrained by a government during civil disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: The run TINU sits inside 'government in unrest'; 'kept back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is any organised body of soldiers, such as a company or battalion.

clue.text: Nervous characteristic of cricket?

definitions.meaning: the insect cricket leaps about, rather than the British bat-and-ball game

explanation.definitionFit: Jumpy means on edge, and also literally describes a leaping insect such as a cricket.

clue.text: Musical group finding port after time

indicators.note: after says the port comes behind the time letter

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A band discovers a harbour town after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three musicians playing together.

clue.text: John Prescott's first circular manoeuvre

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, which in Britain is a loo

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the following name

explanation.surface: A move made by the British politician John Prescott.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was a British Deputy Prime Minister; 'John' is the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a manoeuvre in which a plane flies a full circle, so it is a circular manoeuvre.

clue.text: Resounding noise that may introduce foxtrot?

definitions.meaning: a sound reflected back off a surface
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for E comes just before Foxtrot for F

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a reflected sound and is also the radio code word for E, which precedes F.

clue.text: Slippery customer that'll give you a squeeze and take you out?

definitions.text: Slippery customer that'll give you a squeeze and take you out?

parts.words: Slippery customer that'll give you a squeeze and take you out?
parts.note: it reads like a shifty date who hugs you and takes you out, but a huge snake squeezes and kills its prey

explanation.definitionFit: A large South American snake kills prey by coiling round and crushing it.

clue.text: Trap a couple that's disrupted legal body

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snare set for a pair has upset the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A court hearing appeals against lower courts' decisions is a judicial body.
